design.question: Can a linked account preserve bodily-case variation, need for judgment, advisers' prior experience and the reader's trust instruction without turning testimony into the reader's own observation or an infallible outcome?

design.input: Variable bodily cases motivate a need for judgment; a described adviser group has much prior experience.
carried_dependencies: The adviser noun phrase supplies the referent for den in the trust instruction.
The adviser group owns the past experience; the human reader receives the directive.
Earlier old/young recipients and later old/grey advisers share an age descriptor without establishing identical individual referents.
design.written_output: The reader is instructed to believe the described experienced advisers. The source does not report completed belief, name every advised proposition, or establish successful treatment.
proposed_construction: Preserve role/referent reset and the later anaphoric link; no unconditional truth-transfer rule.
design.distinguishing_consequence: A source account may assert advisers' past experience and a directive to the reader without attributing those observations to the reader, making belief already actual, identifying an old patient with an adviser, or certifying every statement of every physician. A mere response-variation account omits the written downstream anaphoric trust instruction and its group antecedent.
rivals: Generic bodily variation with no referenced adviser group.
Speaker's personal experience silently owns all third-person predicates.
Authority implies universal truth or treatment success.
An old patient becomes the adviser by shared age wording alone.
The admonitory fool phrase is a clinical two-class treatment rule.
interpretive_costs: Experience-to-trust is a reason-giving sequence, not a measured reliability coefficient.
Exact coordinated/genitive grouping of the advisers remains qualified; no rigid modern professional-set intersection is forced.
